examples.solution_text:
Follow the sloping arm to the outer scale that starts at zero on the right.
It crosses one small interval after $60^{\circ}$, so the angle is $65^{\circ}$.
The other scale reads $115^{\circ}$ and starts at zero on the left, so it is the wrong scale here.

Use the inner scale, which starts at zero on the left.
Follow the other arm to $140^{\circ}$.
The outer-scale reading is $40^{\circ}$, but that scale starts at zero on the right.

(a) Place the centre on the vertex and zero along the horizontal arm. Follow the other arm: $49^{\circ}$.
(b) Line up the protractor in the same way. The second reading is $126^{\circ}$.
The second angle is larger because $126>49$.

Measure the smaller turn first: $128^{\circ}$.
The smaller turn and the reflex turn make a full turn.
$360^{\circ}-128^{\circ}=232^{\circ}$.
The marked reflex angle is $232^{\circ}$.

examples.question_text: A protractor gives paired readings $48$ and $132$. The angle is obtuse. Which reading is correct? Explain your check.
examples.solution_text:
An obtuse angle is larger than $90^{\circ}$ and smaller than $180^{\circ}$.
The correct reading is $132^{\circ}$. The paired reading $48^{\circ}$ is acute, so it comes from the wrong scale.

examples.question_text:
(a) A student places the protractor centre $1$ cm away from the vertex. Explain how to correct the setup.
(b) A student writes an angle measurement as $74$. Correct it and explain the symbol.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Move the centre onto the vertex and line the zero mark up with one arm. Otherwise the other arm crosses the scale at the wrong place.
(b) Write $74^{\circ}$. The symbol $^{\circ}$ means degrees.
